title: Heart motif — lacy
subtitle: A filet-crochet heart with a picot border, 9 cm wide in 4-ply cotton
excerpt: The lacy heart works the same two-lobe construction as the basic heart, but with an open filet-mesh interior and a picot-edged border. In 4-ply cotton on a 2.5 mm hook it measures 9 cm and reads as a delicate lace motif. Used as a Valentine's window hanging, gift tag embellishment, and fine-gauge shawl scatter.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 5 (1890), filet lace heart chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet filet heart and love token.
heroPrompt: A crochet lacy heart in white 4-ply cotton with a filet-mesh interior and picot-scallop border, 9 cm wide, photographed on a deep pink background in soft daylight.

chartDefinition.title: Heart motif — lacy
chartDefinition.caption: Two lobe half-circles as for basic heart. Interior replaced with ch-2 mesh rows. Picot border around the outside edge.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three chains closed back into the first chain with a slip stitch. Adds a small decorative scallop loop — used here around the entire outer heart border.

content.text: The lacy heart uses the same two-lobe joining construction as the basic heart, but the interior rows are worked as a dc-ch2-dc filet mesh rather than solid dc rows. The outer edge adds a
picot
border — one dc, one picot, repeating around the outer curve and down to the V-point. The picots along the V-point are smaller (ch-2 instead of ch-3) to give a tighter point.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 4 g of white or pink 4-ply cotton. A 2.5 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat and T-pins for the finished piece.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished lacy heart motif measures 9 cm wide and 8 cm tall in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc), dc2tog — UK; US "single crochet / sc2tog".
picot (p) — ch 3, sl st into first ch.
Pattern
Lobes — same as basic heart
Work both lobes exactly as for crochet-themed-heart-basic: two ch-4 ring semicircles with 10dc each.
Interior mesh rows

Join both lobes along the base as for the basic heart. Instead of solid dc rows for the taper, work filet mesh: Ch 3 (counts as dc + ch-1). *Dc in next dc. Ch 2. Skip 1dc.* Repeat across, ending dc. Turn. Repeat for 3 rows, with dc2tog at each end of each row (to form the taper toward the point). On the final row, work dc2tog at the centre 2 stitches to begin forming the V-point. Fasten off.
Picot border

Join yarn at the centre top dip between the two lobes. Work dc and picot (ch 3, sl st into first ch) alternately around the entire outer edge of the heart, including down the sides and around the V-point (using smaller ch-2 picots at the very point for a tighter finish). Sl st to join. Fasten off.

definition.title: Heart motif — lacy
definition.caption: Two 10dc lobes joined at base. Interior: ch-2 filet mesh rows decreasing to V-point. Outer edge: picot border (dc + p alternating).

content.text: Finishing
Pin the finished heart to a blocking mat — pin at the dip between the lobes, at the outermost points of each lobe, and at the V-point tip. Allow to dry fully before removing pins.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Re-pin and block after washing to restore the shape.
What to try next
The basic heart (crochet-themed-heart-basic) is the solid version for a faster make. The cherry blossom (crochet-flower-cherry-blossom) uses the same picot technique at a smaller flower scale.
